contracts.action: Run Cypress through cypress-io/github-action@v7 in the Admin UI E2E matrix job (install: false, browser, wait-on, working-directory js/apps/admin-ui, SPLIT env)
contracts.before_after: Before: the same step used cypress-io/github-action@v6 with identical inputs. After: @v7 with the same inputs; the diff changes only the tag. The workflow has no other use of cypress-io/github-action, so no other caller is affected.
contracts.visible_effect: Cypress runs in the admin-ui-e2e matrix (chrome and firefox, five containers). A failure shows as a failed step and fails the admin-ui-e2e job, which is listed in the status-check job's needs (.github/workflows/js-ci.yml:307, 296-313).
contracts.failure_mode: If v7 changed or removed one of the inputs used here, or its runtime, the step fails in CI and the failure is visible. Nothing is silently lost. The author has not shown from this repository that v7 keeps these inputs; that depends on the action's release notes, which are not in the repository.
contracts.open_question: Do the v7 release notes keep the install, browser, wait-on and working-directory inputs and the Node runtime that the Admin UI E2E job relies on? The PR body is only the Dependabot title, and the release notes are outside the repository. The CI run for this PR is the check that settles it.

summary: Reviewed .github/workflows/js-ci.yml (the only file in this part). The change bumps cypress-io/github-action from v6 to v7 in the Admin UI E2E Cypress step (line 269). It is a Dependabot major bump, and the PR body only says so. The repository pins its other actions by major tag (about 100 occurrences across 22 files), so @v7 follows the convention. The step's inputs (install, browser, wait-on, working-directory) and its env are unchanged. The step's neighbours (pnpm-setup, cypress-cache) install the Cypress binary and Node 22 before it, so nothing in this repository depends on the old tag. No ADRs exist in docs/adr/. I could not check v7's release notes from the repository, so whether its inputs and runtime still match is left as an open question for the CI run, not a finding. No findings.
